MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  FEBRUARY 9,2026
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  5:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Riggins called the meeting to order at 4:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Marianne Riggins; Mayor Pro Tern Bruce Silverstein; and
  Councilmembers Haylynn Conrad, Doug Stewart and Steve Uhring.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Riggins opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: None.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 4:01 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following items listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

Conference with Legal Counsel — Existing litigation pursuant to Government Code Section
54956.9(d)(1):

  1.  Case Name: City's Petition to Form Malibu USD from Territory in the Santa
  Monica-Malibu USD

Conference with Legal Counsel — Anticipated Litigation

  1.  Initiation of litigation pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Government
  Code section 54956.9
  Number of potential cases: (3)

REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Riggins called the meeting to order at 6:02 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of February 9, 2026
  Page 2 of 11

  PRESENT: Mayor Marianne Riggins; Mayor Pro Tern Bruce Silverstein; and
  Councilmembers Haylynn Conrad, Doug Stewart and Steve Uhring.

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Rob DuBoux, Interim City
  Manager; Christopher Smith, Assistant City Manager; Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin
  Riesgo, Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy, Community Development
  Director; Susan Duefias, Public Safety Director; Tatiana Holden, Interim Public Works
  Director; Monica Castillo, Deputy City Attorney; Parker Davis, Media Technician;
  Cynthia Alba, Senior Management Analyst; Greg Kajszo, Assistant to the City Manager;
  Nico Sanchez, Management Analyst; Christina Muiioz, Deputy City Clerk; Jason
  Lawrence, Deputy City Clerk; and Tyler Eaton, Assistant Community Development
  Director.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Mayor Riggins led the Pledge of Allegiance.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attorney Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 4:00 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.9, with all Councilmembers present. He stated the Council discussed the items on
  the Closed Session agenda. He reported Councilmember Conrad recused herself from one
  item for conference with legal counsel regarding anticipated litigation, due to location of
  her home. He reported that by a vote of 5-0, the Council provided direction to initiate an
  action, and that action, the defendants, and other particulars shall, once formally
  commenced, be disclosed to any person upon inquiry unless to do so would jeopardize the
  City's ability to effectuate service on one of the unserved parties or to do so would
  jeopardize the City's ability to conclude existing settlement negotiations to its advantage.
  He stated no other reportable action was taken.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  January 30, 2026, with the amended agenda posted on February 6, 2026.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

  The Council discussed reordering the agenda.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein moved, and Mayor Riggins seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda, hearing Item No. 2.A. before the Consent Calendar and Item
  No. 5.A. before Item No. 4.A. The motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 2  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Presentation of City Tile to Chris Frost for his service on the Public Safety
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of February 9, 2026
  Page 3 of 11

  Commission

  Councilmember Stewart presented the City Tile to Chris Frost in recognition of his
  service on the Public Safety Commission.

  Mr. Frost discussed his years of service and thanked the Council for the recognition.

ITEM 1  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Public comments: none.

  Item No. 1.B.4 was pulled by the Council.

MOTION  Councilmember Stewart moved, and Councilmember Uhring seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar, pulling Item No. 1.B.4. The motion carried
  unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Waive Further Reading
  Recommended Action: After the City Attorney has read the title, waive full
  reading of ordinances considered on this agenda for introduction on first
  reading and/or second reading and adoption.
  2.  Approve Warrants
  Recommended Action: Allow and approve warrant demand numbers
  77869-77976 on the register from the General Fund and direct the City
  Manager to pay out the funds to each of the claimants listed in Warrant
  Register No. 783 in the amount of the warrant appearing opposite their
  names, for the purposes stated on the respective demands in a total amount
  of $2,115,002.18. City of Malibu payroll check number 5557-5559 and
  ACH deposits were issued in the amount of $596,023.10.
  3.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the July 10, 2025 Special
  Meeting.
  5.  Retired Annuitant Extra-Help Agreement for Gigi Decavalles-Hughes
  Recommended Action: 1) At the recommendation of the City Manager,
  approve the appointment of Gigi Decavalles-Hughes pursuant to
  Government Code Section 21224; and 2) Authorize the City Manager to
  execute the retired annuitant extra-help agreement with Ms. Decavalles-
  Hughes.

  The following items were pulled from the consent calendar for individual consideration:

  4.  Park Enhancement and Donation Program
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of February 9, 2026
  Page 4 of 11

  Recommended Action: At the recommendation of the Parks and Recreation
  Commission, approve revisions to the Park Enhancement and Donation
  Program.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Councilmember Conrad moved, and Councilmember Uhring seconded a
  motion to approve revisions to the Park Enhancement and Donation
  Program. The motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 2  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  B.  City Council Reorganization

  1.  Presentations to Outgoing Mayor

  Mayor Pro Tem Silverstein presented the outgoing Mayor award to Mayor
  Riggins.

  2.  Remarks by Outgoing Mayor

  Mayor Riggins reflected on her term as Mayor and thanked her family for
  supporting her service. She thanked the residents for electing her to serve
  as Councilmember.

  Councilmember Uhring, Councilmember Stewart, and Councilmember
  Conrad commended Mayor Riggins for her service as Mayor.

  3.  Election of Mayor

  Mayor Riggins opened the floor for public comment.

  George Lance indicated he intended to speak on general public comment.

  Zak Gaidzik, Los Angeles County Supervisor Horvath's Office, thanked
  Mayor Riggins for her service and presented a commendation on behalf of
  Supervisor Horvath.

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Riggins returned the matter
  to the table for discussion.

  Mayor Riggins opened the floor to nominations for Mayor.

MOTION  Councilmember Stewart moved, and Mayor Riggins seconded a motion to
  nominate Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein for Mayor. The motion carried
  unanimously.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of February 9, 2026
  Page 5 of 11

  4.  Election of Mayor Pro Tern

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor for public comment. As there were no
  speakers present, Mayor Silverstein returned the matter to the table for
  discussion.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to nominations for Mayor Pro Tem.

MOTION  Mayor Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Riggins seconded a motion
  to nominate Councilmember Miring for Mayor Pro Tern. The motion
  carried unanimously.

  5.  Administration of Oath of Office to Newly Elected Mayor and Mayor Pro
  Tern

  Louis Silverstein administered the oath of office to Mayor Silverstein.

  City Clerk Pettijohn administered the oath of office to Mayor Pro Tern
  Uhring.

ITEM 3  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  Kevin Shenkman, Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission (MPRSC),
  discussed the Commission's work on proposed amendments to the Mobilehome
  Ordinance and expressed concerns regarding staffs recommendation. He
  recommended the proposal be reviewed by the MPRSC Ad Hoc Committee and the
  City Council's Mobilehome Park Rent Control Regulations Ad Hoc Committee.

  In response to Mayor Silverstein, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated the Council
  could continue Item No. 5.A. to a future meeting.

  Mayor Silverstein asked the crowd to indicate if they wanted the item to be
  continued.

  Mayor Silverstein indicated support for hearing the item tonight.

  Scott Dittrich, Public Works Commission, commended Mayor Silverstein, Mayor
  Pro Tern Uhring, and Mayor Riggins for their service. He discussed the Public
  Works Commission's consideration of the Las Flores and Rambla Pacifico
  intersection realignment. He commended Chris Frost for his service on the Public
  Safety Commission.

ITEM 2  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  B.  City Council Reorganization

  6.  Remarks by Newly Elected Mayor
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of February 9, 2026
  Page 6 of 11

  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein discussed his campaign platform and ongoing
  commitment to transparency, accountability, and ethics.

ITEM 3  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  Interim City Manager DuBoux discussed the Los Angeles County emergency rent
  relief program for tenants and landlords affected by recent emergencies. with
  applications accepted until March 11, 2026. He provided an update on the
  skatepark, and announced a soft opening was scheduled for February 14, 2026. He
  discussed the Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) Signal Synchronization project ribbon
  cutting held the previous week, the Malibu High School project, the Southern
  California Edison undergrounding project, Caltrans work on PCH, the upcoming
  rain event He provided a report on, and rebuild permit statistics. He commended
  Community Development Director Bundy for her work on rebuild permits.

  Assistant City Manager Smith discussed the required financial notice recently
  published in The Malibu Times. He announced that the full mid-year budget report
  would be heard on February 23, 2026. He discussed the City's fund balances and
  expenditures, the projected recovery arc from the Franklin Fire and Palisades Fire,
  and expected disaster reimbursement.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, presented the
  January 2026 crime statistics. He presented a video of a news reports regarding fatal
  collisions on PCH and Malibu Canyon Road. He announced an upcoming DUI
  checkpoint. He discussed reports of theft of construction supplies in the burn area
  and encouraged property owners to file letters of agency with the Sheriffs
  Department.

  The Council directed questions to Sergeant Soderlund.

ITEM 5  ORDINANCES AND PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  Proposed Amendments to the Malibu Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization
  Ordinance
  Recommended Action: 1) After the City Attorney reads the title of the ordinance,
  introduce on first reading Ordinance No. 532, an ordinance of the City of Malibu
  amending Chapter 5.16 (Mobilehome Park Rent Control Regulations) of Title 5
  (Business Licenses and Regulations) and repealing Chapter 2.28 (Mobilehome Park
  Rent Stabilization Commission) of Title 2 (Administration and Personnel) of the
  Malibu Municipal Code, and finding the ordinance is exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act; and 2) Direct staff to schedule second reading and
  adoption of Ordinance No. 532 for the February 23, 2026 City Council Regular
  Meeting.

  Interim City Manager DuBoux, Deputy City Attorney Castillo, and City Clerk
  Pettijohn presented the staff report.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of February 9, 2026
  Page 7 of 11

  The Council directed questions to staff.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: Candace Bowen Ferguson, and Leslie Starus

  The Council directed questions to Ms. Starus.

  Speakers: Marti Maniates-Casorla, and Finn Hinke

RECESS  At 8:05 p.m., Mayor Silverstein recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 8:15
  p.m. with all Councilmembers present.

  Speakers: Kelly McKinna, Bracken Carter, Lydia Graham, Diane Klein, Monica
  DeMoulin, Chris DeMoulin, Arpie Petkus (Barbara Fish, Ali Moses, K. Suder,
  Leila Furman, Margaret Jolley deferred time to Arpie Petkus), Kevin Shenkman
  (Bill Sampson deferred time to Kevin Shenkman), Marielle Hadid, Steven Stein,
  Ken Kravenas, Ren Smith (Meghan Rostaysky, Mary Kumble, Abby Wolf,
  Michelle Weiss, Whitney Chiate deferred time to Ren Smith), Stacy Clunies-Ross
  (Robert Webster deferred time to Stacy Clunies-Ross), McCallum Webster, Steve
  Dahlberg, Gary Springer, Mads Jorge (Sal Fish, Shelley Schuster, Maria Altobello,
  Ryan Whalley deferred time to Mads Jorge), Andres Springer, Heather Michael.
  Dru Ann Dixon-Jacobson, and Stefen Lipofsky

  The Council directed questions to Mr. Lipofsky.

  Speakers: Sophia Springer, Katarina Vinegrad, Geoffrey Ortiz, Travis Springer,
  Marty King, LaRonda Rogers, A.J. Rogers, Laura Rosenthal (Lonnie Weinstork,
  Valentina Sartorius deferred time to Laura Rosenthal), Jo Drummond, and Andy
  Lyon

  Jeff Jennings, Jonathan Davidorf, Zippora Karz, Romy Rapoport, Jody Helfend,
  and Ivette Helfend were not present at the time of the hearing.

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Silverstein returned the matter to
  the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Mayor Silverstein moved, and Mayor Pro Tern Uhring seconded a motion to direct
  staff and the Mayor and Mayor Pro Tern to work with California Strategies to
  oppose AB 768. The motion carried unanimously.

  The Council discussed the item.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of February 9, 2026
  Page 8 of 11

MOTION  Councilmember Stewart moved, and Mayor Pro Tern Uhring seconded a motion to
  direct that, through its rulemaking power, all regulations of the Mobilehome Park
  Rent Stabilization Commission in place on June 1, 2025, remain in effect and the
  operative regulations of the Commission unless and until a new Ordinance is
  adopted by the City Council or further direction is given by the City Council.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Mayor Silverstein moved to add direction the Commission to review regulations
  regarding hearing procedures consistent with the current ordinance and make
  recommendations to the Mobilehome Park Rent Control Regulations Ad Hoc
  Committee for review.

  The amendment was accepted by the maker and the seconder.

  The amended motion carried unanimously.

MOTION  Councilmember Stewart moved, and Mayor Silverstein seconded a motion to table
  consideration of Ordinance No. 532 and directed the City Council Mobilehome
  Park Rent Control Regulations Ad Hoc Committee to review the ordinance.

RECESS  At 10:35 p.m., Mayor Silverstein recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at
  10:45 p.m. with all Councilmembers present.

MOTION  Councilmember Stewart moved, and Mayor Silverstein seconded a motion to hear
  Item No. 8.A next and after 10:30 p.m. The motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 8  COUNCIL ITEMS

  A.  Council Appointment to the Public Safety Commission
  Recommended Action: Councilmember Stewart to make a new appointment to the
  Public Safety Commission.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment. As there were no speakers
  present, Mayor Silverstein returned the matter to the table for discussion.

  Councilmember Stewart appointed Meril Maye to the Public Safety Commission.

MOTION  Councilmember Riggins moved, and Councilmember Stewart seconded a motion
  to hear Item No. 6.A. next and after 10:30 p.m. The motion carried 4-1, Mayor
  Silverstein opposed.

ITEM 6  OLD BUSINESS

  A.  Update on Temporary Use and Sign Permit Regulations and Consideration of
  Zoning Text Amendment
  Recommended Action: 1) Receive update on the implementation of Ordinance No.
  526, amendments to Temporary Use Permit (TUP) and Sign Permit regulations to
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of February 9, 2026
  Page 9 of 11

  support economic recovery following the impacts of the 2025 Palisades Fire; 2)
  Adopt Resolution No. 26-06, initiating a Zoning Text Amendment (ZTA) to Title
  17 (Zoning) of the Malibu Municipal Code (MMC) related to TUP and Sign Permit
  regulations; 3) Bypass the Zoning Ordinance Revisions and Code Enforcement
  Subcommittee (ZORACES) review; and 4) Direct the Planning Commission to
  schedule a public hearing regarding the same.

  Assistant Community Development Director Eaton presented the staff report.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.

  Speaker: Molly Scott

  Rafi Antely was not present at the time of the hearing.

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Silverstein returned the matter to
  the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item.

MOTION  Councilmember Riggins moved to: 1) adopt Resolution No. 26-06, initiating a
  Zoning Text Amendment (ZTA) to Title 17 (Zoning) of the Malibu Municipal Code
  (MMC) related to TUP and Sign Permit regulations; 2) bypass the Zoning
  Ordinance Revisions and Code Enforcement Subcommittee (ZORACES) review;
  and 3) direct the Planning Commission to schedule a public hearing regarding the
  same.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Mayor Silverstein seconded the motion and moved to direct the Planning
  Commission to provide a recommendation on the effective period for the ordinance
  and the calendar and period of time for a TUP in response to the request from the
  Boys and Girls Club.

  The maker accepted the amendment.

  The amended motion carried unanimously.

MOTION  Mayor Silverstein moved, Mayor Pro Tern Uhring seconded a motion to hear Item
  No. 4.A. after 10:30 p.m. The motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 4.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Norm Haynie commended Chris Frost for his service.

  Kevin Keegan discussed the upcoming 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles,
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of February 9, 2026
  Page 10 of 11

  the opportunities for the City, and requested the Council direct staff to schedule an
  item for March or April to discuss 2028 Summer Olympics.

  Joella Lee discussed unsafe school bus stops in the City, including at Winding Way.

  Cici Lee discussed the pink rosy trumpet tree in the Civic Center and recommended
  improving the soil to improve the health of the tree. She suggested a location for a
  horse trail and additional trees.

  Heather Michaels deferred time to Jo Drummond.

  Jo Drummond discussed fire recovery, the President's Executive Order regarding
  rebuilding permitting, and the proposed Council Policy to Facilitate the
  Expeditious, Efficient and Economical Rebuild of all Structures in the City
  Destroyed or Materially Damaged by Wildfire, Earthquake, Flood, Landslide,
  Mudslide or Similar Disaster. She requested the Council adjourn in memory of
  Steven Rouse.

  Daniel Smith discussed issues with trash collection charges showing up on bills for
  fire damaged properties.

  Andy Lyon requested accountability from staff regarding the removal of the
  temporary skatepark for the permanent skatepark construction. He discussed the
  permanent construction and the surplus process for the temporary skatepark
  equipment. He also discussed skaters using the permanent park while it was still
  under construction.

  Colin Drummond congratulated Mayor Silverstein and Mayor Pro Tern Uhring and
  thanked Councilmember Riggins. He stated he attended the PCH Signal
  Synchronization Ribbon Cutting. He requested an update on the speed cameras.
  He discussed speeding in the 25 MPH zone on PCH.

  Anne K. and Bill Sampson were not present at the time of the hearing

  In response to Councilmember Stewart, Interim City Manager DuBoux stated staff
  was negotiating with the vendor for the speed cameras and the item was tentatively
  scheduled for March 23, 2026.

  In response to Councilmember Conrad, Interim City Manager DuBoux explained
  that the revenue generated from the tickets will offset the costs of the speed camera
  program. He stated staff would look into the Winding Way bus stop issue.

ITEM 4.B.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  This item was not heard and continued to the February 23, 2026 Regular Meeting.

ITEM 7  NEW BUSINESS
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of February 9, 2026
  Page 11 of 11

  None.

ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Silverstein adjourned the meeting at 11:33 p.m. in memory of Steven Rouse and
  Hunter Langley.

  Approved and adopted by the City Council of the
  City of Malibu on August 24, 2026.

  BRUCE S  RSTEIN, Mayor
